zones.pattern: Any new Postgres `numeric` column will come back from `pg`/Kysely as a JS string, not a number, unless a type parser is registered for OID 1700. Already hit and fixed once for `products.capacity` via `types.setTypeParser(1700, parseFloat)` in client.ts. If a future numeric column doesn't behave as a real `number` at runtime despite the Kysely type saying `number`, check this type-parser registration first before assuming a repository or contract bug.

zones.pattern: Repository port interfaces and record types must live in their OWN module's domain/ports.ts, never get appended to a neighboring module's ports file for convenience. This actually happened once: Machine's port/record ended up inside modules/catalogue/domain/ports.ts during initial Step 4 work and had to be moved into modules/equipment/domain/ports.ts. It directly undermines the reason catalogue and equipment were split into two modules (catalogue must stay ownerless/platform-level with no knowledge of org-owned entities). When reviewing a new port, check the file path it landed in, not just whether the interface content is correct.

zones.pattern: Fastify 5's `setErrorHandler` defaults its error-type generic to `unknown` unless explicitly set (e.g. `setErrorHandler<FastifyError>(...)`, importing `FastifyError` from "fastify"). A plain `(error, request, reply) => {...}` handler that accesses `error.statusCode`/`error.code` outside an `instanceof AppError` branch will fail `tsc --noEmit` with TS18046. This was introduced during an earlier logout-bug fix and went unnoticed for multiple sessions because typecheck verification was repeatedly scoped to `packages/contracts` only, never the full `apps/api` package. Always run `pnpm --filter @fleetip/api run typecheck` (not just the contracts one) before calling API-side work verified.

zones.pattern: An application service returning a repository Record directly (snake_case: created_at, organization_id, product_category_id, ...) instead of mapping it to the matching camelCase contract type from packages/contracts ships a response that silently doesn't match its own Zod schema. This actually shipped once: CatalogueService/EquipmentService both returned raw *Record objects straight from the repository, and it was only caught by an actual HTTP round-trip test (curl against a running dev server), not by typecheck/lint/unit tests — none of those layers verify the HTTP response body's real shape. The existing correct precedent was already in the codebase (AuthService.getAuthenticatedSession manually maps membership rows to camelCase) but wasn't followed when the two new services were written. Fix pattern: a small `toX(record): ContractType` mapper per entity, with the service method's return type explicitly annotated as the imported contract type (e.g. `Promise<Product[]>`) so a missing/misnamed field becomes a compile error next time instead of a silent runtime shape mismatch. When adding a new service, always do one real HTTP call against it, don't rely on `tsc`/tests alone to prove the response shape is right.

zones.pattern: `legalNextStatuses()` in this file is a deliberate, small duplication of the server's `canTransition()` state-machine rule (apps/api/src/modules/equipment/domain/machine-status.ts), used only to decide which status-change buttons the UI offers. Do not "fix" this duplication by importing server domain logic into the browser bundle, and do not assume the UI rule is the source of truth — `canTransition` on the server remains the sole enforcement point and must be updated first if the state machine ever changes; this client copy just needs to be kept in sync manually.

zones.pattern: In an async React event handler, never read `event.currentTarget` after an `await` — React nulls it out once the synchronous part of the event dispatch finishes, so `event.currentTarget.reset()` (or any other access) throws "Cannot read properties of null" post-await. Capture the element into a local variable (e.g. `const formElement = event.currentTarget`) before the first `await`, then use that local everywhere after. In `handleRegister` this bug also silently broke the follow-up `refreshMachines()` call: the throw happened on the line right before it, so newly-created machines never appeared in the list even though the POST had actually succeeded (surfaced as a generic "Cannot read properties of null" error).

zones.pattern: Tailwind v4's automatic content scan (in `apps/web`, whose only CSS entry is `apps/web/app/globals.css`) does not reach into `packages/ui/src` on its own, even though Next's `transpilePackages` makes that package's TSX source get bundled into the app's JS. Any utility class used ONLY inside a `@fleetip/ui` component (and nowhere in `apps/web`'s own `.tsx` source) is silently dropped from the compiled CSS — no error, no warning, the class just never renders. Caught this by grepping the served `/_next/static/css/app/layout.css` for classes unique to `EmptyState`/`LoadingState`/`ErrorState` (`border-dashed`, `animate-spin`, `border-red-200`) and finding them absent, while classes that happened to also appear in an `apps/web` file (e.g. `shadow-sm`, `rounded-full`) were present and gave a false sense that scanning was working. Fixed with an explicit `@source "../../../packages/ui/src";` line in `globals.css`, right after `@import "tailwindcss"`. Rule of thumb: any time a Tailwind-styled component lives in a workspace package outside the consuming app's own directory tree, verify its classes actually made it into the compiled CSS by grepping the served stylesheet for a class unique to that component — don't assume Tailwind's content scan crosses workspace-package boundaries on its own.

zones.pattern: Adding a new permission code to `permissionCodeSchema` + `PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES` (the contracts-level declaration) does NOT make that permission real in the database — the actual `permissions` table row and the `role_permissions` grant to `owner` are a separate, easy-to-forget step. Confirmed live: `rental.manage` was added to both contracts constructs in Step 2, but every single Rental E2E request (even from a legitimate Rental Company owner) 403'd until a dedicated seed migration (mirroring 0005's `equipment.manage` grant exactly) actually inserted the `permissions` row and the `role_permissions` link. `PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES`'s `Record<PermissionCode, ...>` completeness check (Step 1's safety net) catches a missing *organization-type* entry at compile time, but has no way to catch a missing *database seed* — that gap is invisible to `tsc`, only shows up as a live 403. Rule for the next new permission: after adding it to the contracts enum + type map, always add the matching `permissions`/`role_permissions` seed migration in the same pass, and verify with one live request before considering the permission "done" — don't rely on typecheck passing as proof it works.

zones.pattern: When a new PermissionCode is added to PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES, AuthService.getAuthenticatedSession's per-membership `permissions` array (returned by /auth/me) must filter each role-granted code through PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES[code].includes(organizationTypeCode) — it previously just returned every permission the role grants (roleRepository.listPermissionCodesByRoleId), unfiltered by the membership's actual organization type. Caught live during Auction/RFQ E2E testing: a Renter's own /auth/me response listed rental_company-only codes (equipment.manage, rental.manage, auction.participate, quotation.manage) it could never actually exercise (PermissionService.hasPermission still correctly denied them — this was a display/nav-menu correctness bug, not an authorization hole). Fixed by filtering the list against PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES using row.organization_type_code before returning it. Any future change to PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES or to how memberships are listed should re-verify this filter is still applied.
